901.219(2)(b)(iii).text: the procedures set out in the RPAS operations manual; and

901.219(2)(c).text: a process for assessing the competency of each person who receives training and for evaluating the effectiveness of the training program.

901.219(3).text: An RPAS operator shall ensure that any training provided to meet the requirements of this section is based on the content of the RPAS operator’s training program.

901.219(4).text: No RPAS operator shall permit a person to act, and no person shall act, as an instructor unless

901.219(4)(a).text: the person has demonstrated to the RPAS operator knowledge of the content of the RPAS operations manual; and

901.219(4)(b).text: in the case of a flight training instructor, the person holds the pilot certificate required by this Part in respect of the operations to be conducted.

901.219(5).text: No RPAS operator shall permit a person to act, and no person shall act, as an instructor unless the person has received, before the day on which the person begins to act as an instructor, training that includes the following elements:

901.220(1).text: An RPAS operator shall appoint a person responsible for RPAS maintenance.

901.220(2).text: The person responsible for RPAS maintenance shall plan and oversee the maintenance of the RPAS operator’s remotely piloted aircraft systems, including coordinating maintenance arrangements with third-party maintenance providers.

901.221(1).text: An RPAS operator shall establish and maintain a maintenance control manual that includes

901.221(1)(a).text: the name of every person authorized by the RPAS operator to perform maintenance actions;

901.221(1)(b).text: any records referred to in paragraph 901.223(1)(e); and

901.221(1)(c).text: procedures for servicing, maintenance and pre-flight and post-flight inspections of the RPAS operator’s remotely piloted aircraft systems that are consistent with any instructions from the manufacturer.

901.221(2).text: The RPAS operator shall ensure that the maintenance control manual is made available to the Minister on request.

901.222.text: An RPAS operator shall designate a pilot-in-command for each operation conducted under Division VI.

901.223(1).text: Every RPAS operator shall keep the following records:

901.223(1)(a).text: a record containing the names of the pilots, pilots-in-command and other crew members who are involved in each flight and, in respect of a remotely piloted aircraft system, the time of each flight or series of flights;

901.223(1)(b).text: a record containing the names of the employees, the agents or mandataries and the representatives of the operator;

901.223(1)(c).text: a record containing the names of every person who has received training provided by the operator and the nature of that training;

901.223(1)(d).text: a record containing the registration numbers of all remotely piloted aircraft it operates; and

901.223(1)(e).text: a record containing the particulars of any mandatory action and any other maintenance action, modification or repair performed on a remotely piloted aircraft system, including

901.223(1)(e)(i).text: the names of the persons who performed them,

901.223(1)(e)(ii).text: the dates on which they were undertaken,

901.223(1)(e)(iii).text: in the case of a modification, the manufacturer, model and a description of the part or equipment installed to modify the system, and

901.223(1)(e)(iv).text: if applicable, any instructions provided to complete the work.

901.223(2).text: Every RPAS operator shall ensure that the records are made available to the Minister on request and are retained for a period of

901.223(2)(a).text: in the case of the records referred to in paragraphs (1)(a), (b) and (c), 12 months after the day on which they are created; and

901.223(2)(b).text: in the case of the records referred to in paragraphs (1)(d) and (e), 24 months after the day on which they are created.

903.01.text: No person shall conduct any of the following operations using a remotely piloted aircraft system unless the person complies with the provisions of a special flight operations certificate — RPAS issued by the Minister under section 903.03:

903.01(a).text: the operation of a remotely piloted aircraft having an operating weight of more than 150 kg (331 pounds);

903.01(b).text: the operation of a remotely piloted aircraft having an operating weight of less than 250 g (0.55 pounds) at an advertised event; and

903.01(c).text: any other operation of a small remotely piloted aircraft or medium remotely piloted aircraft for which the Minister determines that a special flight operations certificate — RPAS is necessary to ensure aviation safety or the safety of any person.

903.02(1).text: For the purpose of an application for a special flight operations certificate — RPAS, the operation, other than for the purpose of providing a commercial air service, of a remotely piloted aircraft system that includes a remotely piloted aircraft that is not registered in accordance with Division III is a very low-complexity operation.

903.02(2).text: For the purposes of an application for a special flight operations certificate — RPAS, the operation of a remotely piloted aircraft system at an advertised event is a low-complexity operation.

903.02(3).text: For the purpose of an application for a special flight operations certificate — RPAS, the following operations are medium-complexity operations:

903.02(3)(a).text: the operation of a remotely piloted aircraft having an operating weight of more than 150 kg (331 pounds);

903.02(3)(b).text: the operation by a person described in subsection 900.09(2) of a remotely piloted aircraft system for the purpose of providing a commercial air service;

903.02(3)(c).text: the operation, for the purpose of providing a commercial air service, of a remotely piloted aircraft system that includes a remotely piloted aircraft that is not registered in accordance with Division III;

903.02(3)(d).text: the operation of a remotely piloted aircraft at an altitude greater than one of the altitudes referred to in subsection 901.25(1), unless the operation at a greater altitude is authorized under subsection 901.71(2);

903.02(3)(e).text: the operation of more than five remotely piloted aircraft at a time to conduct a VLOS operation, or the operation of more than one remotely piloted aircraft at a time to conduct an operation that is not a VLOS operation, from a single control station; and

903.02(3)(f).text: the operation of a remotely piloted aircraft outside of Canadian Domestic Airspace.

903.02(4).text: For the purpose of an application for a special flight operations certificate — RPAS, the following operations are high-complexity operations:

903.02(4)(a).text: the operation of a remotely piloted aircraft system without the pilot or a visual observer having the aircraft in visual line-of-sight if the operation is not a sheltered operation or an extended VLOS operation conducted under Division V or a BVLOS operation conducted under Division VI;

903.02(4)(b).text: the operation of a remotely piloted aircraft to transport any of the payloads referred to in subsection 901.43(1);

903.02(4)(c).text: the operation of a remotely piloted aircraft to conduct a BVLOS operation within five nautical miles of an aerodrome that is listed in the Canada Flight Supplement or the Water Aerodrome Supplement;

903.02(4)(d).text: the operation, in weather conditions that do not meet the conditions set out in section 901.34, of a remotely piloted aircraft to conduct a BVLOS operation or of a medium remotely piloted aircraft to conduct a VLOS operation;

903.02(4)(e).text: the operation of a remotely piloted aircraft that carries persons on board; and

903.02(4)(f).text: any other operation of a remotely piloted aircraft system for which the Minister determines that a special flight operations certificate — RPAS is necessary to ensure aviation safety or the safety of any person.

903.02(5).text: If the application for a special flight operations certificate — RPAS is in respect of several operations, the highest complexity level applies except in the case of an application in respect of two or more medium-complexity operations, in which case the application is deemed to be in respect of a high-complexity operation.

903.02(6).text: A person who proposes to operate a remotely piloted aircraft system to conduct very low-complexity or low-complexity operations shall apply to the Minister for a special flight operations certificate — RPAS by submitting the following information:

903.02(6)(a).text: the legal name, trade name, if any, address and contact information of the applicant;

903.02(6)(b).text: the means by which the person responsible for the operation can be contacted;

903.02(6)(c).text: the operations for which the application is made;

903.02(6)(d).text: the manufacturer and model of the system and the registration number, if any, referred to in paragraph 900.16(3)(a);

903.02(6)(e).text: the pilot certificate number issued to any crew member; and

903.02(6)(f).text: any other information requested by the Minister pertinent to the safe conduct of the operations.

903.02(7).text: A person who proposes to operate a remotely piloted aircraft system to conduct medium-complexity or high-complexity operations shall apply to the Minister for a special flight operations certificate — RPAS by submitting the following information:

903.02(7)(a).text: the legal name, trade name, if any, address and contact information of the applicant;

903.02(7)(b).text: the means by which the person responsible for the operation can be contacted;

903.02(7)(c).text: the operations for which the application is made;

903.02(7)(d).text: the manufacturer and model of the system and the registration number, if any, referred to in paragraph 900.16(3)(a), as well as a complete description of the remotely piloted aircraft that is an element of the system, including its performance, operating limitations and equipment;

903.02(7)(e).text: a detailed plan describing how the operations are to be carried out;

903.02(7)(f).text: a risk assessment for the operation that accounts for both ground and air risks;

903.02(7)(g).text: the pilot certificate number issued to any crew member or a description of the means by which the applicant will ensure that all crew members hold the necessary certificates and qualifications;

903.02(7)(h).text: the standard procedures for crew members in the case of operations requiring more than one crew member;

903.02(7)(i).text: the instructions for maintaining the system in a state that is fit and safe for flight;

903.02(7)(j).text: the type, manufacturer, model and operating limitations of the detect and avoid system to be used, if any, and the procedures respecting the detection and avoidance of conflicting air traffic and other hazards; and

903.02(7)(k).text: any other information requested by the Minister pertinent to the safe conduct of the operations.

903.02.1(1).text: The holder of a special flight operations certificate — RPAS may apply to the Minister to amend the certificate to change

903.02.1(1)(a).text: the dates and alternate dates of the operations;

903.02.1(1)(d).text: the pilot certificate number issued to a crew member;

903.02.1(1)(e).text: the type, manufacturer, model and operating limitations of the detect and avoid system to be used and the procedures respecting the detection and avoidance of conflicting air traffic and other hazards; and

903.02.1(1)(f).text: in the case of a certificate in respect of an operation set out in subsections 903.02(1) or (2), the manufacturer and model of the remotely piloted aircraft system and the registration number referred to in paragraph 900.16(3)(a).

903.02.1(2).text: An application to amend a special flight operations certificate — RPAS shall include the following information:

903.02.1(2)(b).text: the validity period of the certificate; and

903.02.1(2)(c).text: the change that is the subject of the application.

903.03.text: The Minister shall, on receipt of an application submitted in accordance with section 903.02 or 903.02.1, issue or amend a special flight operations certificate — RPAS if the applicant demonstrates to the Minister the ability to perform the proposed operations without adversely affecting aviation safety or the safety of any person.

903.04.text: A special flight operations certificate — RPAS shall contain the following information:

903.04(a).text: the name and address of the certificate holder;

903.04(c).text: the date of issue of the certificate;

903.04(d).text: the validity period of the certificate;

903.04(e).text: the type of operations authorized; and

903.04(f).text: any condition pertaining to the operations that the Minister considers necessary for aviation safety or the safety of any person.
